entities.name: VCAN
observations: V0/V1 versican isoforms were identified as glioma-derived factors and were highly expressed in mouse and human glioma tissue.
Glioma-cell VCAN knockdown reduced microglial MT1-MMP, intracerebral tumor size, and mouse mortality; microglia were required for the ex vivo growth effect.

entities.name: TLR2
observations: Recombinant VCAN V1 induced MT1-MMP in wild-type but not Tlr2-knockout microglia.
TLR2-neutralizing antibody reduced glioma-induced microglial MT1-MMP and organotypic glioma growth; TLR2 was increased in glioma-associated microglia but not astrocytes.
In a separate study, Tlr2 deficiency reduced GL261 tumor growth and prolonged survival.

entities.name: MT1-MMP
observations: Microglial MT1-MMP is a downstream effector associated with VCAN-TLR2-driven glioma expansion and is reduced by VCAN knockdown or TLR2 blockade.

entities.name: Glioma
observations: The relevant causal evidence comes mainly from mouse intracerebral glioma implants and organotypic brain-slice cultures; human evidence is mainly tissue expression.
The VCAN-TLR2 pathway is supported as contributory, but clinical dominance and uniform effects across infiltrating macrophages remain unproven.
